name: Management company profits

subjectOf.text: Of those who responded, 75.4 percent indicated that the profits of their investment management company were affected by the new registration and disclosure requirements, consistent with the management company, rather than the fund, bearing most of those costs.
subjectOf.abstract: 75.4% indicated that the profits of their investment management company were affected. This is consistent with anecdotal evidence suggesting that it is the investment management company that bears the majority of costs associated with the registration and disclosure requirements.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915
scope_conditions: supported by anecdotal evidence on cost allocation

subjectOf.text: By 2015 a clear majority of respondents, 93 percent, attributed effects on their investment management company's profits to additional expenses associated with the Dodd-Frank Act, and no respondent reported no additional expenses, compared with 19 percent in 2012.
subjectOf.abstract: Figure 19 illustrates that a clear majority of respondents in 2015 (93%) be- lieved that the profits of their investment management company were affected by additional expenses associated with the Dodd Frank Act.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Post Dodd-Frank Act Evolution of the Private Fund Industry Comparative Evidence from 2012 and 2 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2739479
scope_conditions: survey respondents reporting on management company profits
